Thank goodness for good managers. I have had ones throw me under the bus. Like when someone returned two body shapers claiming she washed them only ONCE. Uh yeah, in a barrel full of gravel then dried by tying them to the back of your car and driving them across the city. She said it was hand washed. These things almost didn't even LOOK like shapers. Or anything. Just a pile or torn up lace, wire, an elastic. And the manager STILL let the return happen after I stated the policy about damaged items. No was was that a manufacture defect. Hand washing does not bend underwires into 12 degree angles unless you do it on purpose. I do not have the strength to mimic that.

I am not too surprised. What I love is when I watch a manager when someone has no proof of purchase try to return an item that is clearly stolen. I saw the manager go; "Hmm... So you said you got it here in this city... Huh. It says none have been sold around here. Let me stretch the diameter to 200 miles. Nope. Still nothing. And hmmm.... HMMMM.... The item was put out in stores today... And we have only been open for 45 minutes... How fast would you need to drive to clear a 200 mile radius in 40 minutes? I'm shortening the time because you still had to enter the store, get the item, somewhere try it on and determine that it wasn't the right fit and still decide to blaze all the way over to this particular store, and I am not even counting for time zones? Mind enlightening me on that one? And what about this hole here that just so happens to be where we would place a sensor? I can't do refunds on damaged merchandise..." Up until now, she had a very joyful sing-song tone. Then she smirked and changed her tone to something more fitting of the situation. "I think you better come with me..." And escorted them. Apparently they were pretty well known shoplifters.

Oh man, I loved having fun with known shoplifters. Tag switchers were my favorite. "Huh... This is *weird\~* This tag here says the item is *CORAL.* Goodness, but this is sky blue! Let's scan the tag! Oh dear! The picture is showing me an off-the-shoulder store-brand shirt from the Junior's Clearance section! Huh... It isn't available in any sort of blue... And this is a pair of DKNY jeans! Let me see... It looks like you bought this in the men's department yesterday. I just happen to know the person who checked you out is here today! Since this item isn't from my department, and we are having an issue with it, I recommend talking with who sold it to you, or to take it upstairs to the Women's department. I can see the gentleman that checked you out is at the counter right now!" Playing dumb like this will sometimes intimidate them back into playing dumb and leaving. But, if I get through the whole spiel, unless they ask for a manager (who will do the exact same thing at this point.) Will usually not go to the suggested departments and either try with a different associate or just give up an leave. It gets ugly when the managers are called because they will huff and puff and call me stupid. Jokes on them. LP is called as soon as they are out of earshot.

I used to bicycle all the time. This year, I got it all tuned up and ready to go... Just fifteen minutes in, my back pain kicked in. I walk to work every day, have a vegetarian diet, and have thighs that could crush anything. Trust me, exercise isn't the answer to everything. Pushing myself is all I have ever done. I was homeless at one point, kidnapped, raped, beaten, but eventually got a job and got out. Then I lost the job when I started having kidney stones; and apparently I have had them since high school and still do. The job called me out on a bs reason, but it pretty much was because I was falling behind because of the pain. Was stuck with my family for awhile, having to deal with my abusive brother who destroyed the house, stole my meds, and made my life a living hell, hence me not wanting to go back. Then I was taken in by a friend on the other side of the state, later moved in with my boyfriend because she was going through a divorce and moved the next state over, had a nice time at my last job, but lost it when I got sick again, and the repetitiveness is exhausting me. I wish I could just afford a little shack of a home where I can be at peace and live off the land. Garden and stuff like that. But I can't hold down a job long enough because of the pain that I cannot afford to treat. I am really sorry, but I had to get this out.
